headline: Cloud infrastructure surges, but margins keep compressing
summary_short: Akamai's Q1 FY2026 revenue was $1.074 billion, up 6% y/y, led by 40% growth in Cloud Infrastructure Services, while GAAP diluted EPS fell 13% y/y to $0.71 and operating income fell 26% y/y to $114.5 million.
summary_long: Revenue grew 6% y/y to $1.074B: Cloud Infrastructure Services rose 40% to $95M and Security rose 11% to $590M, offset by a 7% decline in Delivery revenue to $389M. GAAP operating income fell 26% y/y to $114.5M (margin -4ppt to 11%) as costs grew faster than revenue; a lower tax rate (13% vs 29%) cushioned net income to -14% ($106.3M) and diluted EPS to -13% ($0.71). Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.61, -5% y/y. Cash fell to $622.4M from $1.097B on $205.9M buybacks and $191.8M capex. Akamai disclosed a new $1.8B, seven-year CIS commitment from a frontier AI model provider. Guidance: Q2 revenue $1.075-$1.100B, non-GAAP EPS $1.45-$1.65; FY2026 revenue $4.445-$4.550B, non-GAAP EPS $6.40-$7.15.

drivers.explanation: Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue rose 40% y/y to $95M and Security rose 11% to $590M, partially offset by a 7% y/y decline in Delivery and other cloud applications to $389M.
Not explicitly attributed in the release; cost of revenue, R&D, and S&M expense each grew faster y/y than the 6% revenue growth, compressing GAAP operating margin by 4ppt to 11%.
Net income fell a smaller 14% than operating income's 26% drop because the GAAP effective tax rate fell to 13% from 29% a year earlier, partially offsetting the lower pretax income.

CEO cited a new commitment from a leading U.S.-based frontier AI model provider of $1.8 billion over seven years for Cloud Infrastructure Services, calling it validation of Akamai's position in the AI economy.
